_comment: Bean d5f1. One agent's INSPECTION of every extracted image, as data rather than code, so the judgement can be reviewed line by line and re-run. `saw` is the REASON for the role, not the description; `draft` is the description. Every entry here was produced by looking at the image. Applied by scripts/apply-image-verdicts.ts, which writes an `inspection` basis naming this agent and leaves every narrative in `draft` — only a human may confirm one (schemas/narrative.ts). SPLIT 2026-09-20 (bean frs5): this file judged documents that now live in TWO libraries, so it became two files, each beside the documents it judges. A single verdict file spanning libraries is how one library's judgement comes to rewrite another's `images.json` -- `apply-image-verdicts` resolves each document against the library its verdict file is IN, and could not do that from one shared file. Nothing was re-judged: every verdict below is byte-identical to the one it was split from, and `inspected_by`/`inspected_at` are carried over unchanged because the inspection they record actually happened, once, before the split. ADDED 2026-09-29: verdicts for arxiv-2601.22554v1, arxiv-2406.01940v2 and arxiv-2602.16554v1, each produced by opening the image. The file-level `inspected_at` still names the milnorlink inspection because the schema carries one date per file; the three arXiv documents were inspected on 2026-09-29, and this sentence is where that is recorded rather than restamping milnorlink's date. ADDED 2026-10-12 (owner ruling 2026-10-12, litlfred/qou#7735): verdicts for arxiv-2003.08005v1, arxiv-2512.09874v3 and arxiv-2604.00554v1, 34 images, all `figure`. Carried byte-for-byte from litlfred/qou library/image-verdicts.json at commit 2bd612e3ef (PR litlfred/qou#7608, bean qou-v9av), where each was produced by an agent (claude-opus-5-5) opening the image on 2026-10-11; nothing was re-judged here. As with the 2026-09-29 additions, the file-level `inspected_by`/`inspected_at` still name the milnorlink inspection, and this sentence is where the later inspection is recorded.

img-p008-1.saw: Figure 2(a), the blueprint dependency graph of the multivariate Taylor case study, the initial blueprint drafted by the language model
img-p008-1.draft: Figure 2(a): the first blueprint produced for multivariate Taylor's theorem in integral form, before any automated proving. Rectangles are definitions and ellipses are theorems; dashed arrows mark a statement-level use and solid arrows a proof-level use. Definition nodes taylorKernel, taylorRemainderKernel, taylorPoly, lineMap and lineCurve sit at the top; the target frechet_taylor_integral is the sink at the bottom. Most theorem nodes are light blue (unproved); only taylor_integral_one_shot, integrationByParts_smul and ftoc_bochner_wrapper are dark green.

img-p008-2.saw: Figure 2(b), the same graph after the automated prover's first pass
img-p008-2.draft: Figure 2(b): the same initial blueprint after the automated prover's sorry-filling pass. Rectangles are definitions and ellipses are theorems; dashed arrows mark a statement-level use and solid arrows a proof-level use. Definition nodes taylorKernel, taylorRemainderKernel, taylorPoly, lineMap and lineCurve sit at the top; the target frechet_taylor_integral is the sink at the bottom. The leaf lemmas taylorKernel_deriv_t, taylorKernel_at_right and taylorRemainder_eq_explicit have turned dark green; taylor_integral_kernel and lineCurve_iteratedDeriv remain light blue, and taylor_integral_explicit and frechet_taylor_integral are filled a lighter green; the caption distinguishes only blue (unproved) from green (proved), so what the two shades of green separate is not stated in the paper.

img-p008-3.draft: Figure 2(c): the refined blueprint after the planner model decomposed the stuck nodes further. Rectangles are definitions and ellipses are theorems; dashed arrows mark a statement-level use and solid arrows a proof-level use. Definition nodes taylorKernel, taylorRemainderKernel, taylorPoly, lineMap and lineCurve sit at the top; the target frechet_taylor_integral is the sink at the bottom. New intermediate nodes appear -- taylor_remainder_by_parts, taylor_integral_kernel_base, taylorPoly_succ, ftoc_bochner_on_uIcc and lineCurve_contDiffOn_onSeg -- and every theorem node is light blue, i.e. nothing is yet proved in this version.

Definition nodes taylorKernel, taylorRemainderKernel, taylorPoly, lineMap and lineCurve sit at the top; the target frechet_taylor_integral is the sink at the bottom. Nearly every lemma is dark green; three remain light blue -- taylor_remainder_by_parts, lineCurve_iteratedDeriv and frechet_taylor_integral -- which are the nodes the text says were left for a human. taylor_integral_kernel, taylor_integral_explicit and taylor_integral_one_shot are a lighter green.
